title: Find One First
child_idea: When we know what a group costs, we can find what one costs by sharing equally. Then we can find what any number of them cost.

topics: Multiplication and division word problems: divide within 20, multiply within 40 (Primary 1, Multiplication and Division, p. 31)
Count money in dollars (Primary 1, Money, p. 31): whole dollars only, no notes, coins or cents until Term 3
moe.note: Strand label for the tutor only. This is an added lesson (gap from the word-problem books analysis: the price or size of one from a group). Start here is Primary 1 content: share a total equally to find one (within 20), then multiply to find many (within 40), in whole dollars. BEYOND PRIMARY 1 ON PURPOSE: Think harder and Go further chain the two steps with different numbers (the price of 7 from the price of 3), use the words a dozen and such, ask how many can be bought, and compare the price of one in two shops. Owner decision, 22 Oct 2026: strong content with scaffolding, said plainly to families. Say this on the parent page and in the opening of the guide; do not describe the lesson as MOE-aligned or syllabus-aligned. Money is only whole dollars and $1 tokens (counters): no notes, coins or cents until Term 3. Vocabulary taught here: each, a dozen, such. This lesson also holds Mi's Challenge Quest (20 minutes, minutes 35 to 55; a game with Mi, not a test); the tutor notes with the private notes sheet and the grown-up note are in the Quest files built by assets/quest_build.py. Contest tag (tutor only): price of one first, then many; how many can be bought; compare the price of one.

objectives: Find the cost of one by sharing a total equally ("4 pens cost $20, so 1 pen costs $5") and the cost of many from the cost of one ("1 pen costs $3, so 4 pens cost $12").
Draw a strip of equal parts for the story and write both steps: find one first, then find many.
Use the words each, a dozen and such.
Think harder: find the price of 7 from the price of 3, use a dozen and such, and say how many can be bought.
Go further: one price from each of two groups, money left over, and which shop sells one for less.
Play Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi on private paper: 8 short gates that visit the lessons of the term.

slides.subtitle: Find one, then find many

mascot.say: Hi, I'm Mi. Let's notice, test and explain why!

slides.title: Warm-up: share equally

blocks.text: Deal the counters one at a time. Same number on each plate.

slides.note: Twelve counters are shared equally onto 3 plates. Children deal counters one at a time (or imagine it). Ask: how many on each plate (4); 6 counters shared between 2 plates (3); 15 counters shared among 3 plates (5). Children answer aloud or with fingers. No writing, no marks. A child who is unsure deals real counters or small things onto three plates or three pieces of paper.

slides.title: Each and in all

blocks.text: Each bag has the same number.

slides.note: Three bags with 4 counters in each bag. We say each bag has 4, and in all means every bag together. Ask: how many counters in all (12); 5 bags with 2 in each bag (10); 4 groups of 5 (20). This is Term 2 Lessons 5 and 8 taught again. A child who is unsure adds one bag at a time and says the total each time.

slides.title: A strip of equal parts

blocks.text: 4 equal parts. The whole strip is 20.

slides.note: A strip is cut into 4 equal parts, and the whole strip is 20. Ask: how big is each part (5); 3 parts of 5 (15); 6 shared into 2 equal parts (3). This is Term 2 Lesson 8 taught again: a strip shows equal groups. A child who is unsure counts 5, 10, 15, 20 on fingers and counts the fingers.

slides.title: Sneak-peek puzzles

blocks.text: Ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start. Nobody is judged.

cols.head: PUZZLE 1: anyone can try
items: 4 pencils cost $8.
How much does 1 pencil cost?
You may use counters.

cols.head: PUZZLE 2: think
items: 3 apples cost $6.
How much do 5 apples cost?

slides.note: Puzzle 1 (4 pencils for $8; 1 pencil is $2) is an access question: any child can share 8 counters onto 4 pencils. Puzzle 2 is a thinking question on the lesson idea: find one first. 1 apple costs $2 and 5 apples cost $10. Say: two sneak-peek puzzles, ideas we have not learnt yet; a guess is a great start and I do not know is welcome; nobody is marked. Children write on their own paper. Nobody holds paper to the camera. There is no private chat. Answers: $2; $10. Do not reveal puzzle 2 until Talk time. Do not write scores or keep a list.

slides.title: Explore: find one

items: 4 pens cost $20. Count out 20 tokens.
Share the tokens equally onto 4 pens.
How much does 1 pen cost?

slides.note: Round 1, about 4 minutes. Children use their $1 tokens (the kit page or counters) and 4 small things as the pens. 4 pens cost $20: they count out 20 tokens and deal them one at a time onto the 4 pens until every pen has the same. Ask: how much does 1 pen cost (5). Say: 1 pen costs $5, because $20 shared equally among 4 pens is $5 each. Money is whole dollars only, and a token stands for $1. If a family has no shop items, 4 pieces of paper are fine. Answer: $5.

slides.title: Find many

items: 1 pen costs $3. Put 3 tokens by each pen.
Do this for 4 pens.
Count all the tokens.

slides.note: Round 2, about 3.5 minutes. Now we know the cost of one: 1 pen costs $3. For 4 pens children put 3 tokens by each pen and count all the tokens (12). Ask: how much do 4 pens cost (12). Say: 4 groups of $3 is $12. Link to Term 2 Lesson 5: groups of. Answer: $12. A child who loses count puts the tokens in a row of 3 and counts in 3s.

slides.title: Find one, then many

items: 4 pens cost $20.
How much do 3 pens cost?
Find 1 pen first: share $20 into 4 equal parts.
Then take 3 parts.

slides.note: Round 3, about 3.5 minutes. 4 pens cost $20. How much do 3 pens cost? Children share 20 tokens onto 4 pens (5 each) and then take 3 pens (15). The strip shows 4 equal parts for the 4 pens, and 3 parts are the 3 pens. Ask: how much does 1 pen cost (5); how much do 3 pens cost (15). Say: find one first, then find many. Answers: $5 and $15. The steps (find 1 pen first, then take 3 parts) appear on the next slide, after the children have tried.

slides.title: Find one first

blocks.head: STEPS
items: Step 1: find 1. Share the cost equally.
Step 2: find many. Count that many ones.

slides.note: 5 cups cost $15. How much do 2 cups cost? Step 1 finds 1 cup: $15 shared equally among 5 cups. Step 2 finds 2 cups: 2 groups of that. Ask: how much does 1 cup cost (3); how much do 2 cups cost (6). The steps card appears on the next slide, after the children have answered. Children say each number first. Always say find one first.

slides.title: Write the two steps

rows: 2 cups: 2 groups of the cost of 1 cup
head: Step
What we do
Cost in $

blocks.text: Check: 5 cups at $3 each make $15.

slides.note: Write the two steps: Step 1 is 15 shared equally among 5, which is 3. Step 2 is 2 groups of 3, which is 6. Check by putting the cost of one back: 5 groups of $3 is $15. Say each step as a short sentence. Either reading order of a groups line is accepted in a child answer. Answers: $3 and $6.

slides.title: Three words
slides.note: Three words for word problems. Each means for one. A dozen is 12. Such means of the same kind, so 6 such cups are 6 cups the same, with the same price. Ask: what is a dozen (12); a dozen eggs is how many eggs (12); if 3 such cups cost $6, does each cup cost the same (yes). A dozen and such are used in Think harder.

slides.title: A dozen

blocks.text: A dozen cookies is 12 cookies.

slides.note: Count the cookies together: 12. A dozen is 12, whatever it is 12 of. A dozen eggs, a dozen pens. Ask: how many pens are in a dozen (12). This slide is optional to shorten: cut it first if the Mini-lesson runs over.

slides.title: Your turn

blocks.text: How much does 1 pencil cost? How much do 4 pencils cost?

slides.note: Each child works on their own paper with tokens if they like. 6 pencils cost $18. Step 1: 1 pencil costs $3. Step 2: 4 pencils cost 4 groups of $3, which is $12. Walk the cameras; do not ask children to hold papers up. Wait 10 seconds before helping. Answers: $3 and $12.

slides.title: Check: your turn
slides.note: Answers: 1 pencil costs $3 and 4 pencils cost $12. Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Children tick their own work with a tick. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

slides.title: Move and count

blocks.text: Count in twos. Stamp for each one.
Count in fives. Clap for each one.
Stand up. Sip some water.

slides.note: Four minutes. Stand up on camera. Count in twos to 20 and stamp softly on each number, then count in fives to 40 and clap on each number. No equipment, no running, a little clear space. A child may stay seated and tap the table. Do not give prizes or compare children. Then ask everyone to take out the closed Quest Log and a pencil, ready for Mi's Challenge Quest.

slides.title: Talk and explain

blocks.head: AISHA SAYS
items: 3 books cost $12.
So 6 books cost $24.

blocks.text: Is Aisha right? How could we check?
I think ... because ...

slides.note: One minute of talk to the grown-up next to you, or to your screen. Children test Aisha with tokens: 12 tokens on 3 books is 4 each, and 6 books at 4 each is 24; or 6 books are 2 lots of 3 books, so 2 lots of $12. Then volunteers first; a pass is always fine; never call a child by name to answer. Model answer: yes. 1 book costs $4, so 6 books cost 6 groups of $4, which is $24. Repeat each child answer in your own words for the recording.

investigation.title: Which pack costs less?
investigation.first: A pack of 2 pens costs $8. How much does 1 pen cost?
investigation.text: A pack of 5 pens costs $20. Does 1 pen cost less in this pack? Why?
investigation.answer: No. In both packs 1 pen costs $4 ($8 shared between 2 pens, and $20 shared among 5 pens), so 1 pen does not cost less in the bigger pack. Finding the price of one lets us compare packs of different sizes.
investigation.look_for: A child who finds $3 for both packs, or who says 1 pen costs the same in both. Credit any clear reason. A child who says the bigger pack costs more is right about the total but has not compared one pen.
mistakes: Saying 1 pen costs less in the pack of 5 because it has more pens.

The group plays it in pairs (a child and a quest partner) or as a group quest with Mi, on private paper. No score or mark is shown to the child, there is no ranking and no visible timer. The tutor keeps private notes only, for one line to each grown-up and for advice for next term's group. It keeps the 20-minute slot after the break and the question quality: 8 short gates and one optional secret cave item, all at Start here level. Term 2 Lessons 3 and 4 share gate 3 and Term 2 Lessons 5 and 6 share gate 4, so every lesson of the term is still visited. Gate 7 asks the child to try a friend's number by putting it back, which is the claim-trying the term line talks about. A middle child needs about 17 minutes of reading aloud and quiet work; a slower child may use a few minutes of the workbook time to finish. The quest sits straight after the brain break (not at the end of the lesson as in Term 1) so children are fresh. The Quest Log has no pictures except the ten-frames in gate 3, because the page generator draws only a few figure types.
challenge_quest.story: Mi the dolphin is swimming to the Pearl Cave. Eight gates are in the way, and each gate has one puzzle. At the end there is an optional secret cave.
child_rules: Mi is swimming to the Pearl Cave and needs your help at 8 gates.
Work on your own paper. Your quest partner sits beside you: talk about how, then write your own answer.
It is not a race and nobody sees your answers. You may skip a gate: Mi swims round it.
You may use counters or your fingers.
The secret cave at the end is optional, just for fun.
challenge_quest.child_footer: Math Inquirers Term 2 Mi's Challenge Quest. Print at 100% (actual size).
page_instructions: Gates 1, 2 and 3: Mi needs your help. Write your answers in the spaces.
Gates 4, 5 and 6: keep swimming. Write your answers in the spaces.
Gates 7 and 8 and the secret cave: nearly there. Circle Yes or No where you see it.

questions.skill: A place in a line (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and how many are in front
questions.text: Siti is 4th in a line. Ben stands right behind Siti.

parts.text: There are [box] children in front of Siti.

questions.say: Gate 1. Siti is 4th in a line. Ben stands right behind Siti. Part a: Ben is blank in the line. Part b: how many children are in front of Siti?
questions.solution: Right behind the 4th child is the 5th. In front of Siti are the 1st, 2nd and 3rd children: 3 children.
questions.right: Both correct (5th or 5 is right for part a).

questions.skill: A strip for more: the other person and the total
questions.text: Ravi has 26 marbles. Lily has 9 more marbles than Ravi.
questions.say: Gate 2. Ravi has 26 marbles. Lily has 9 more marbles than Ravi. Part a: Lily has blank marbles. Part b: they have blank marbles altogether.
questions.solution: Lily has 9 more than Ravi, so add: 26 + 9 = 35. Altogether: 26 + 35 = 61.
questions.partly: Part a right and part b wrong, or part b right from a wrong part a (counts as one).

questions.skill: A double from ten-frames (Term 2 Lesson 3) and odd or even (Term 2 Lesson 4)
questions.say: Gate 3. Look at the ten-frames: 9 and 9. Part a: 9 plus 9 equals blank. Part b: write odd or even. 15 is blank.
questions.solution: 9 + 9 = 18 (one ten-frame is filled with 9, and so is the other: 10 + 8). 15 pairs up with 1 left over, so 15 is odd.
mistakes: (b) even (the last digit 5 is not read).

questions.skill: Groups of the same size and the times sign (Term 2 Lesson 5), counting in 2s (Term 2 Lesson 6)
questions.text: Jenny has 3 jars. Each jar has 5 sweets.
questions.say: Gate 4. Jenny has 3 jars. Each jar has 5 sweets. Part a: fill in the boxes: blank times blank equals blank. Part b: count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, blank, 10.
questions.solution: 3 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, so 3 × 5 = 15 (5 × 3 = 15 is also right). Counting in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
questions.right: Both correct (3 and 5 in either order, and 15).
questions.partly: One of the two correct, or the product right with the factors swapped or missing.

questions.skill: Share equally and put into groups (Term 2 Lesson 7)
questions.text: Siti shares 16 stickers equally among 4 friends. Kumar puts 10 pens into boxes, 2 pens in each box.

parts.text: Each of Siti's friends gets [box] stickers.

questions.say: Gate 5. Siti shares 16 stickers equally among 4 friends. Kumar puts 10 pens into boxes, 2 pens in each box. Part a: each of Siti's friends gets blank stickers. Part b: Kumar needs blank boxes.
questions.solution: 16 shared equally among 4 friends is 4 each. 10 pens in groups of 2 make 5 boxes (2, 4, 6, 8, 10).

questions.skill: A times story with a second step (Term 2 Lesson 8)
questions.text: Mei has 5 bags. Each bag has 3 sweets. She gives 4 sweets to Ben.
questions.say: Gate 6. Mei has 5 bags. Each bag has 3 sweets. She gives 4 sweets to Ben. Part a: the bags have blank sweets. Part b: Mei has blank sweets left.
questions.solution: 5 groups of 3 is 15 sweets. She gives 4 away: 15 - 4 = 11.
questions.partly: Part a right and part b wrong (for example 19), or part b right from a wrong part a.

questions.skill: A hidden number in a picture equation, and checking a friend's number (Term 2 Lesson 9)
questions.text: Each shape is a number. The heart + the heart = 18. Ben says the heart is 8.

parts.text: Is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No. [yesno]

questions.say: Gate 7. Each shape is a number. The heart plus the heart equals 18. Ben says the heart is 8. Part a: is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No. Part b: the heart is blank.
questions.solution: 8 + 8 = 16, not 18, so Ben is not correct. 9 + 9 = 18, so the heart is 9.

questions.skill: Find one first, then many (Term 2 Lesson 10)
questions.say: Gate 8. 8 buns cost 16 dollars. Part a: 1 bun costs blank dollars. Part b: 5 buns cost blank dollars.
questions.solution: $16 shared equally among 8 buns is $2 each. 5 buns cost 5 groups of $2, which is $10.
questions.partly: Part a right and part b wrong, or part b right from a wrong part a.

optional.skill: Queue counting: 8th from the front and from the back, and checking a claim
optional.text: Think harder (optional). Ravi is 8th from the front and 8th from the back of a line. Mei says there are 16 children in the line.

parts.text: Is Mei correct? Circle Yes or No. [yesno]
There are ___ children in the line.

optional.say: The secret cave has one more puzzle, and it is optional. You may skip it. Ravi is 8th from the front and 8th from the back of a line. Mei says there are 16 children in the line. Is Mei correct? Circle Yes or No. Then write how many children are in the line.
optional.answer: No; 15 children (7 in front of Ravi, Ravi, and 7 behind him)
optional.solution: There are 7 children in front of Ravi and 7 behind him, and Ravi himself: 7 + 7 + 1 = 15. 8 + 8 = 16 counts Ravi twice.
optional.note: Never marked and never counted. Whether the child tried it adds one neutral phrase to the line for the grown-up; a skipped cave adds nothing.

give: A week before: send the grown-up note (L20_Quest_Parent_Note.pdf) and the Quest Log (L20_Quest_Log.pdf, 3 pages) with the lesson materials. Families print the Quest Log at 100%, keep it closed in an envelope and find a quest partner (a grown-up or a brother or sister). A family with no printer tells you: arrange another way (for example the make-up slot).

Tell the group in the opening and at slide s-quest1: this is Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi. Everyone works on their own paper with a quest partner beside them. It is not a race, a gate may be skipped, and nothing is shown to the group.

Start at minute 35 (straight after the brain break) and finish by minute 55. Children open the Quest Log only when you say. The paper lies flat on the table and is never held up. The quest partner may talk about how to start and ask 'how do you know?', but does not give answers. Cameras may be on or off. Use your own watch out of sight of the camera: no clock, countdown or timer is ever shown to the children.

Read each page aloud, one gate at a time (the script has the words), then leave quiet working time: about 3 minutes for page 1, 3.5 for page 2 and 4 for page 3. After each page say that the gates are open and Mi swims on, whatever the answers. Say nothing about right or wrong, and read no answers. A middle child needs about 17 minutes in all; a slower child may finish in the first minutes of the workbook.

Allowed: fingers, counters and talk with the quest partner. Not allowed: a calculator, a grown-up giving answers, looking at the workbook. A child who finishes early turns the Quest Log over and draws quietly.

After page 2, take a one-minute stretch (stand, shake out, sip water). After page 3, show slide s-quest2. Do not collect or look at any Quest Log. While children work, notice (do not write on the shared screen) how they start: counters, drawing, strip, talking to the partner.
after: Same day: the grown-up takes ONE clear photo of each of the 3 pages (page flat, taken straight from above, the whole page in view, and the name on each page) and sends them to the program's business WhatsApp, +65 9880 5962, and to no other number. Never to a child, never to a personal phone, never into the class chat.

Within 3 days: open the photos only on the business WhatsApp (never on a personal phone) and write your private notes (section 5) for each child, from the photos and what you saw on camera. Section 4 shows what each answer tells you; accept 5 or 5th for gate 1 part a, and either order of 3 and 5 in gate 4. Nothing is written on the child's paper, nothing is added up and no order of children is made. Nothing about the quest goes back to the child or the group except thanks.

Write ONE line for each grown-up from your notes (section 7): what we saw, in plain words, and one small next step if it helps. It is sent to the parent only. No marks, no x out of 8, no ranking, no comparison with other children, no prediction.

Fill in the group advice sheet (section 6): what several children were still working on, with no names, and what you will do in the first lessons of next term. It is kept for next term's tutor and is never shown to families.

Once the line is sent, save the photos to the program's private file store and delete them from the business WhatsApp chat. The program keeps the photos for 90 days after the program ends, then deletes them, as the privacy notice says. Delete each child's notes sheet when the line is sent (keep only the line in the family file, and the group advice sheet). Never forward the photos or save them to a personal phone or any other device.
At the start of next term say to the whole group: thank you for playing Mi's Challenge Quest; there is nothing to share and nothing to fear. Never name a child or an answer.
late: A child who was away or whose family prefers another time: plays the quest at the make-up slot BEFORE watching the recording (the quest is not on the recording, so no gate is given away). It is a small group or a pair with Mi, with a parent beside the child on camera. The tutor never sits alone with one child on a private call.

A child who joined late: the family may choose to leave out gates for lessons the child did not attend. Write nothing for those gates; if no gate of an area was taught, the line for the grown-up says nothing about that area.
A family that does not want the quest: no problem. The child does the Term 2 Lesson 10 work as usual and the line for the grown-up uses your own notes from the lessons only.
A child who is upset or stuck: remind the group (open session) that every gate can be skipped and Mi swims round it. Do not single the child out. The grown-up may stop the quest at any time.

A family with no printer: tell the family to say so a week before and arrange another way (for example the make-up slot, with the Quest Log sent to the family another way). Never ask a child about it in front of the group.
privacy_checklist: Quest Logs are never held up to the camera and never read out.
No answer is said aloud during or after the quest. Gates open for everyone, whatever the answers.
No clock, countdown or timer is shown; nobody is told who finished first or last.

Photos come to the program's business WhatsApp (+65 9880 5962) only; tutors never use a personal phone; photos are kept 90 days after the program ends, then deleted; the line goes to the parent only; no private message to any child.
No score, no x out of 8, no ranking, no tally, no comparison between children, not even in your own notes.

The recording captures the tutor, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted: the recording is paused for the whole quest (slides s-quest1 and s-quest2) and restarted for the workbook. The WhatsApp number is never on a slide.

parent_note.title: Mi's Challenge Quest: a note for grown-ups
parent_note.what: In the last lesson of the term we play Mi's Challenge Quest. Mi the dolphin swims to the Pearl Cave and meets 8 gates, each with a short puzzle, plus an optional secret cave. It takes about 20 minutes, straight after the break. Your child works on private paper with you (or a brother or sister) as quest partner. It is a game: nothing is added up, there is no league table and nobody is compared with anyone else. It helps us see what each child enjoyed and what to practise next. Term 2 goes beyond the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose (odd and even numbers, the 3 and 4 tables, and stories about groups), so a few gates may be new.
before: We send you this note and the Quest Log a week before. Print the Quest Log at 100% (actual size, not fit to page). It has 3 pages. No printer? Tell us a week before and we will find another way.
Keep the Quest Log folded or in an envelope until the tutor says to open it.
Have a pencil, a rubber and a quiet table. Counters and fingers are fine.
during: Be the quest partner: sit beside your child. You may talk about how to start and ask 'how do you know?', but please do not give answers or hints.
Skipping a gate is fine; Mi swims round it. If your child is upset, you may stop at any time.
The paper stays flat on the table. Cameras may be on or off.
after: The same day, take ONE clear photo of each of the 3 pages: page flat, straight from above, the whole page in view. Make sure your child's name is on each page.
Send the photos to the program's business WhatsApp, +65 9880 5962. Please send them to this number only: not to a tutor's own phone, not to the class chat, and never through a child.

We use the photos only to write one line about your child. WhatsApp is a messaging service run by another company. We keep the photos for 90 days after the program ends, then delete them, as our privacy notice says.
parent_note.back: Within a few days we send you ONE line, written from our private notes, about what we saw your child do in the quest, with a small next step if it helps. It only describes what your child did, and it never compares children. If you would rather not play the quest, tell us: that is fine.
